summary: MDC-owned 60-ft steel tower in Sunklands CA, built 1947 or 1950 depending on source; a towerman spotted a 1949 fire; survey finds it standing in fair to good condition.

facts.design: Galvanized steel frame tower with a steel ladder and a pyramid-roofed cab
facts.status_note: Survey (undated in the copy read) says the tower is slated for demolition and recommends documentation as mitigation.

access.note: The tower stands in the Sunklands Conservation Area, open to the public 4:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. No source says whether the tower itself may be climbed.

events.note: Tower site property bought in April 1945 for $2,640, per the survey's summary table.
Survey says the tower was constructed in 1947 (construction date 12/31/47 in MDC files).

Report dated March 17, 1949, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (publication not named there), said the fire blackened a thousand acres of upper Current River country. The Hartshorn towerman spotted a small blaze at 9 p.m. on a Monday, per district forester Lee Fine.
Forest Lookouts page gives 1950 for construction of a 60-foot steel tower. The survey dates construction to 1947.
Entrance road constructed to the tower (fiscal 1950-51).
New anchor bolts placed on the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives 1950 for construction of the 60-foot steel tower. The MDC-based survey says the tower was constructed in 1947, citing MDC files and a 12/31/47 date. The two cannot both be right; the story reports both dates.

Forest Lookouts says a towersite on the Deer Run State Forest was acquired in fiscal 1947-48. The survey says the tower site was bought in April 1945 from W. R. and Audrey Brown. The story reports both dates.

notes_for_editor: The survey PDF is hosted on files.lqdt1.com, a third-party host, and its extracted text has no title, author or date; the 'standing, fair to good' condition comes from it, so confirm the survey's date and origin before publishing. The brief's 18.3 m (60 ft) matches the survey. The Forest Lookouts 1949 fire item is a report quoted on the page; the page does not name its publication, so 'The Index' was dropped from the story. Missouri Life article was blocked (403), so the Hartshorn page's 'Hartshorn towerman' fire report is the only account of the 1949 spotting.
